annotationRationale: Equalizing the amounts requires fraction addition, subtraction, and division by an integer. The mean and linear-equation models are alternative approaches, so their concepts remain method-specific.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Prealgebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The total is 10/3 glasses, so each final share is 5/6 and each donor contributes 1/6. Choice C and the key agree. There are no figure or wording contradictions.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Independently verified and retained both shared methods: 2023_AMC_10B_Q01/find-equal-share and 2023_AMC_10B_Q01/equate-final-amounts. They give useful arithmetic and algebraic approaches. AoPS Solution 2's sixths representation is equivalent arithmetic and needs no separate route.
review.annotationCheck: Fraction addition/subtraction and division by an integer are appropriate assessed concepts. Mean and linear-equation modeling correctly remain method-specific. Empty support and context lists are reasonable.
review.areaCheck: Prealgebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Conservation gives (10/3)/4 = 5/6 per glass, hence a contribution of 1 - 5/6 = 1/6. The receiver also reaches 1/3 + 3(1/6) = 5/6.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly credits 2023_AMC_10B_Q01/find-equal-share and retains both inherited LIVE and AoPS reference IDs. The supplied methodLocalSources supports this reuse. The source-informed-original basis honestly distinguishes project prose and nonofficial references from MAA originals.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Explains why equal sharing uses the total divided by four, establishes the measurement unit, and shows the fraction division explicitly. The explanation is complete for the intended learner.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p129 matches the equal-share mean; cnm_p182 matches division by four; cnm_p173 matches the whole-and-fraction sums and difference. All are supported.
